Anatomy The Circulatory System: Heart, A.question: ১) Which is true end artery?
Anatomy The Circulatory System: Heart, A.exp:
The central retinal artery is a true end artery because it has essentially no significant anastomoses with neighboring arteries. Therefore, its occlusion can cause sudden and severe retinal ischemia and visual loss.

  • Central retinal artery → true end artery

  • Coronary arteries → functional end arteries

  • Splenic artery → has anastomotic circulation

  • Carotid artery → not an end artery

High-yield Anatomy recall:
True end artery → central retinal artery
Functional end arteries → coronary arteries

Exam pearl:
“Retinal artery = true end artery.”

Anatomy The Circulatory System: Heart, A.question: ২) The walls of all four heart chambers consist of ........ major layers?
Anatomy The Circulatory System: Heart, A.exp:
The wall of all four chambers of the heart consists of three major layers:

  1. Endocardium → inner endothelial lining

  2. Myocardium → middle muscular layer responsible for contraction

  3. Epicardium → outer layer (visceral layer of serous pericardium)

High-yield Anatomy recall:
Heart wall = Endocardium + Myocardium + Epicardium

Exam pearl:
“3 layers: Endo → Myo → Epi.”

Anatomy The Circulatory System: Heart, A.question: ৩) Which is not true about veins?
Anatomy The Circulatory System: Heart, A.option2: carry blood from capillaries to heart
Anatomy The Circulatory System: Heart, A.exp:
Veins are generally described as thin-walled, low-pressure vessels that carry blood from capillaries toward the heart. Many veins, especially in the limbs, have valves to prevent backflow.

The statement “have branches” is considered not true in the classical anatomical description because veins are said to have tributaries, whereas arteries branch.

  • Veins → thin-walled

  • Veins → carry blood toward the heart

  • Many veins → have valves

  • Veins → have tributaries rather than branches

Exam pearl:
“Arteries have branches; veins have tributaries.”

Anatomy The Circulatory System: Heart, A.question: ৪) Which is not a component of tunica intima of elastic artery?
Anatomy The Circulatory System: Heart, A.exp:
The tunica intima of an elastic artery consists mainly of:

  • Endothelium

  • Subendothelial connective tissue

  • Internal elastic lamina

Vasa vasorum are small blood vessels that supply the outer part of the vessel wall, mainly the tunica adventitia and outer media. They are not a component of the tunica intima.

High-yield Artery wall recall:
Tunica intima → Endothelium + CT + internal elastic lamina
Tunica media → smooth muscle + elastic fibers
Tunica adventitia → CT + vasa vasorum

Exam pearl:
“Vasa vasorum = mainly adventitia, not intima.

Anatomy The Circulatory System: Heart, A.question: ৫) Which is the thickest histological layer of heart?
Anatomy The Circulatory System: Heart, A.exp:
The myocardium is the thickest histological layer of the heart wall. It is composed mainly of cardiac muscle fibers and is responsible for the contraction and pumping action of the heart.

  • Epicardium → outermost layer

  • Endocardium → innermost lining

  • Myocardium → thickest and muscular layer

  • Subendothelial layer → part of the endocardium

High-yield Heart histology recall:
Endocardium → inner
Myocardium → middle & thickest
Epicardium → outer

Exam pearl:
“Myocardium = thickest layer of the heart wall.”

Anatomy The Circulatory System: Heart, A.question: ৬) Venae comitantes are especially found in .......?
Anatomy The Circulatory System: Heart, A.exp:
Venae comitantes are paired veins that accompany an artery, usually one on each side. They are especially common in the extremities, where they accompany deep arteries and help return blood to the heart through the muscle pump.

  • Extremities → especially common

  • Often accompany deep arteries

  • Pulsations of the accompanying artery help promote venous return

High-yield Anatomy recall:
Venae comitantes = paired veins accompanying arteries → mainly in limbs.

Exam pearl:
“Venae comitantes → deep arteries of the extremities.”

Anatomy The Circulatory System: Heart, A.question: ৭) Large veins have how many layers of smooth muscle?
Anatomy The Circulatory System: Heart, A.exp:
Large veins have a relatively thick tunica adventitia, which contains longitudinal bundles of smooth muscle. These can form more than 5 layers in large veins such as the vena cava.

High-yield Venous histology recall:

  • Large veins → prominent tunica adventitia

  • Adventitia contains longitudinal smooth muscle bundles

  • Tunica media → relatively thin compared with arteries

Exam pearl:
“Large veins → >5 layers of longitudinal smooth muscle in adventitia.”

Anatomy The Circulatory System: Heart, A.question: ৮) What is the location of conducting system of heart?
Anatomy The Circulatory System: Heart, A.exp:
The conducting system of the heart includes the AV bundle (bundle of His), bundle branches, and Purkinje fibers. The Purkinje fibers are located mainly in the subendocardial layer of the ventricles, where they rapidly distribute electrical impulses to the ventricular myocardium.

  • SA node → right atrium

  • AV node → lower interatrial septum

  • Bundle of His → membranous interventricular septum

  • Purkinje fibers → subendocardial layer

High-yield Cardiac conduction recall:
Purkinje fibers = subendocardial location.

Exam pearl:
“Conducting fibers run just beneath the endocardium.”

Anatomy The Circulatory System: Heart, A.question: ৯) Which is not a criteria of heart myocardial tissue?
Anatomy The Circulatory System: Heart, A.exp:
Cardiac muscle has the following characteristic features:

  • Striated banding → present

  • Intercalated discs → present

  • Usually a single, centrally placed nucleus → present

  • Multiple nuclei → not a typical feature

High-yield Cardiac muscle recall:
Cardiac muscle = striated + branched + intercalated discs + central single nucleus.

Comparison:

  • Skeletal muscle → multiple peripheral nuclei

  • Cardiac muscle → 1 (occasionally 2) central nucleus

  • Smooth muscle → single central nucleus

Exam pearl:
“Multiple peripheral nuclei = skeletal; single central nucleus = cardiac.”

Anatomy The Circulatory System: Heart, A.question: ১০) Veins are ......... vessels?
Anatomy The Circulatory System: Heart, A.exp:
Veins are called capacitance vessels because they are highly compliant and can store a large volume of blood at relatively low pressure. They contain approximately 60–70% of the body's blood volume at rest.

  • Veins → capacitance vessels

  • Arterioles → resistance vessels

  • Capillaries → exchange vessels

  • Large arteries → conductance vessels

High-yield Cardiovascular physiology recall:
Arteries → Conductance
Arterioles → Resistance
Capillaries → Exchange
Veins → Capacitance

Exam pearl:
“Veins = volume reservoir = capacitance vessels.”

Anatomy The Circulatory System: Heart, A.question: ১১) Which one collects blood from venules?
Anatomy The Circulatory System: Heart, A.exp:
Small veins (venules → small veins) collect blood from the venules and then drain into medium-sized veins.

Blood flow sequence:

Capillaries → Venules → Small veins → Medium veins → Large veins → Heart

  • Small vein → collects blood from venules

  • Medium vein → receives blood from small veins

  • Large vein → receives blood from medium veins

  • Capillary → connects arterioles and venules

Exam pearl:
“Venules → small veins → medium veins → large veins.”

Anatomy The Circulatory System: Heart, A.question: ১২) The valves of the heart are folds of ....... that enclose a plate like layer of dense fibrous tissue?
Anatomy The Circulatory System: Heart, A.exp:
The heart valves are folds of endocardium that enclose a plate-like layer of dense fibrous connective tissue. This fibrous core provides structural support and prevents the valves from collapsing during cardiac contraction.

  • Endocardium → forms the valve surface

  • Dense fibrous connective tissue → forms the core of the valve

  • Myocardium → responsible for cardiac contraction

  • Epicardium → outer surface of the heart

High-yield Heart histology recall:
Valve = Endocardial fold + dense fibrous connective tissue core.

Exam pearl:
“Heart valves are folds of endocardium.”

Anatomy The Circulatory System: Heart, A.question: ১৩) Vasa vasorum serve a function analogous to that of which of the following?
Anatomy The Circulatory System: Heart, A.exp:
Vasa vasorum are small blood vessels that supply the walls of large blood vessels, particularly the outer parts of the tunica media and adventitia. Their function is analogous to the coronary arteries, which supply blood to the myocardium.

  • Vasa vasorum → supply large vessel walls

  • Coronary arteries → supply the heart muscle

  • Valves → prevent backflow

  • Basal lamina → structural/supportive layer

  • Arterioles → resistance vessels

High-yield Histology recall:
Vasa vasorum = “vessels of the vessels” → nourish large vessel walls.

Exam pearl:
“Vasa vasorum of large vessels are analogous to coronary arteries of the heart.”

Anatomy The Circulatory System: Heart, A.question: ১৪) What tissue is directly associated with and extends into the heart valves?
Anatomy The Circulatory System: Heart, A.exp:
The cardiac skeleton is a framework of dense connective tissue that surrounds the valve openings and extends into the heart valves, providing structural support and anchoring the valve leaflets.

It also:

  • Provides attachment for cardiac muscle fibers

  • Maintains the shape of the valve openings

  • Helps electrically insulate the atria from the ventricles

High-yield Heart anatomy recall:
Cardiac skeleton → fibrous rings around valves + connective tissue extending into valve leaflets.

Exam pearl:
“Heart valves are supported by the fibrous cardiac skeleton.”

Anatomy The Circulatory System: Heart, A.question: ১৫) What do we call the epithelium that lines the blood vessels?
Anatomy The Circulatory System: Heart, A.exp:
Endothelium is a simple squamous epithelium that lines the inner surface of blood vessels and lymphatic vessels. It forms the innermost lining of the vascular system.

  • Endothelium → blood vessels + lymphatics

  • Mesothelium → serous cavities (pleura, pericardium, peritoneum)

  • Epithelioid → describes cells resembling epithelial cells

  • Epithelioma → a type of epithelial tumor

Exam pearl:
“Blood vessel lining = endothelium; serous cavity lining = mesothelium.”

Anatomy The Circulatory System: Heart, A.question: ১৬) Atherosclerosis occurs in ........?
Anatomy The Circulatory System: Heart, A.exp:
Atherosclerosis primarily affects the tunica intima of large and medium-sized arteries. Lipid accumulation, inflammatory cells, and fibrous tissue form atheromatous plaques within the intima.

  • Tunica intima → site of atherosclerotic plaque

  • Tunica media → mainly affected secondarily

  • Tunica adventitia → not the primary site

High-yield Vascular pathology recall:
Atherosclerosis → intimal plaque formation → narrowing of arterial lumen.

Exam pearl:
“Atheroma = Intima.”

Anatomy The Circulatory System: Heart, A.question: ১৭) What type of epithelium lines blood vessels?
Anatomy The Circulatory System: Heart, A.exp:
Blood vessels are lined internally by endothelium, which is a specialized form of simple squamous epithelium.

  • Blood vessels → simple squamous epithelium (endothelium)

  • Mesothelium → simple squamous epithelium lining serous cavities

  • Simple cuboidal → commonly found in renal tubules

  • Simple columnar → commonly found in GI tract

Exam pearl:
“Blood vessels → Endothelium → Simple squamous epithelium.”

Anatomy The Circulatory System: Heart, A.question: ১৮) Which one carry blood back to the heart from microvasculature all over the body?
Anatomy The Circulatory System: Heart, A.exp:
Veins carry blood back to the heart from the microcirculation throughout the body.

Blood flow sequence:

Arteries → Arterioles → Capillaries → Venules → Veins → Heart

  • Arteries → carry blood away from the heart

  • Arterioles → distribute blood to capillaries

  • Capillaries → site of exchange

  • Veins → return blood to the heart

Exam pearl:
“Arteries go away; veins return.”

Anatomy The Circulatory System: Heart, A.question: ১৯) Which is the most prominent feature of elastic arteries?
Anatomy The Circulatory System: Heart, A.option4: adventitia is much thin-ner than the media
Anatomy The Circulatory System: Heart, A.exp:
The most prominent feature of elastic arteries (e.g., aorta and pulmonary trunk) is their thick tunica media, which contains numerous elastic lamellae. These allow the artery to expand during systole and recoil during diastole, helping maintain continuous blood flow.

  • Thick tunica media → characteristic of elastic arteries

  • Vasa vasorum → present, especially in the adventitia and outer media

  • Tunica intima → present but not the most prominent feature

  • Adventitia → thinner than the media

High-yield Artery histology recall:
Elastic artery → thick media + many elastic lamellae → aorta is the classic example.

Exam pearl:
“Elastic artery = thick tunica media with abundant elastic tissue.”

Anatomy The Circulatory System: Heart, A.question: ২০) Which layer in an artery is primarily smooth muscle?
Anatomy The Circulatory System: Heart, A.exp:
The tunica media is the arterial layer primarily composed of smooth muscle cells, along with elastic fibers. Its contraction and relaxation regulate vascular diameter and blood pressure.

  • Tunica intima → endothelium + subendothelial connective tissue

  • Tunica media → mainly smooth muscle

  • Tunica externa/adventitia → connective tissue + vasa vasorum

Exam pearl:
“Tunica media = smooth muscle layer.”
